subtitle: Renderer check for every visual type

slides.title: Flow horizontal: request path
points: Client resolves DNS then opens TCP and TLS
Load balancer picks a healthy pod
NestJS runs middleware, guards, pipes, handler
PostgreSQL answers in 2 ms on a warm cache
slides.example: A 220 ms request spent 90 ms in TLS setup because keep-alive was disabled on the client.
slides.takeaway: Every hop costs a round trip; keep connections alive and measure where the time goes.

slides.title: Flow vertical: event loop phases
points: Timers run first
Then pending callbacks
Then poll for I/O
Then check for setImmediate
Close callbacks last
Microtasks drain between every phase
slides.takeaway: process.nextTick and promises always run before the loop moves on.

slides.title: Stack: reference architecture
points: Stateless API pods behind a load balancer
Redis for cache, locks and rate limits
PostgreSQL is the source of truth
Kafka feeds background workers
slides.example: The same layout served 500 RPS on three pods and one db.r6g.large for a mid-size store.
slides.takeaway: Start with this shape; split services only when a boundary proves itself.

slides.title: Table: isolation levels in PostgreSQL
points: Read Committed is the default and re-reads see new commits
Repeatable Read gives a snapshot per transaction
Serializable detects conflicts and aborts
Retry on 40001 is mandatory at the two upper levels
slides.takeaway: Pick the level per transaction, not per application.

slides.title: Compare: modular monolith vs microservices
points: A monolith can still have hard module boundaries
Microservices buy independent deploys at the price of partial failure
Most teams under 30 engineers ship faster with a monolith
slides.takeaway: Split when a boundary has a different scaling or deploy cadence, not for fashion.

slides.title: Steps: what happens on POST /orders
points: Each step can time out independently
Only the database step holds a connection

items: HTTP request bytes on the wire

slides.takeaway: Trace one request end to end before you optimise anything.

slides.title: Graph: order state machine
points: Only listed transitions are legal
Illegal transitions throw a domain error
Persist every transition in order_events
slides.takeaway: A state machine table beats scattered if-statements every time.

slides.title: Cycle: the debugging loop
points: Mitigate first, then diagnose
Change one thing at a time
Write it down while it is fresh
slides.takeaway: The loop is the method; tools are just accelerators.

slides.title: Code: claim a job with SKIP LOCKED
points: Rows locked by other workers are skipped, not waited on
The UPDATE and the SELECT happen in one statement
Workers never see the same job twice

code.text:
UPDATE jobs SET status = 'RUNNING', locked_until = now() + interval '5 min'
WHERE id = (
  SELECT id FROM jobs
  WHERE status = 'PENDING' AND run_at <= now()
  ORDER BY priority DESC, run_at
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
  LIMIT 1
)
RETURNING *;

slides.example: A 12-worker fleet claimed 4,000 jobs/min from one table with zero duplicates.
slides.takeaway: PostgreSQL is a perfectly good job queue until you need more than ~10k jobs/min.

slides.title: Code: TypeScript transaction with the manager
points: Use the manager passed to the callback, never the injected repository
The callback either commits or rolls back
Keep external calls outside the transaction
slides.takeaway: One transaction, one aggregate, one outbox row.

slides.title: No visual: how a senior thinks about indexes
points: Every index is a tax on every write to that table
Ask which query the index serves and how selective it is
Composite order is equality, then range, then sort
Check pg_stat_user_indexes monthly and drop unused ones
Create with CONCURRENTLY in production, always
slides.example: A 40-index table wrote at a quarter of the speed of the same table with 8 well-chosen indexes.
slides.takeaway: Index for queries you have measured, not for columns you imagine filtering.
